notes: ACCESS: quince.com is directly reachable (HTTP 200 on every page fetched, no WAF/challenge). robots.txt (fetched directly, 2026-08-11) has no Claude-specific 'Disallow: /' - Claude-SearchBot carries the SAME restrictions as the default group (Disallow: /account/*, /accounts/*, /log-in*, /sign-up*, /tracking*, /checkout/thank-you*, /p/*, /partner/*), which per this project's Westwing IT/Noon UAE precedent is NOT a block; none of those disallowed paths were needed for category-page extraction (/shop/home/* is unrestricted). PLATFORM: Next.js SSR with a custom pageDataJson widget tree embedded in __NEXT_DATA__ (widgets[].type=='PRODUCT_LIST', each product card at widgets[].children[].data.productItem, keyed by a stable 'productId'/quince_product_id). Site also runs an Algolia instance (appId K81D2WQH9L, public search key found in page config) for its search bar, index name 'quince_product_color_index' - the index name itself confirms the finding below. CRITICAL COUNT-INFLATION FINDING (this project's first documented case of a non-Shopify per-color-variant duplication pattern): on every Quince category/collection page checked, the site's own rendered 'N items' text and its pagination.total both count ONE ROW PER PRODUCT-COLOR COMBINATION, not one row per distinct product. Verified empirically (not inferred) by parsing the full embedded PRODUCT_LIST widget JSON: e.g. /shop/home/lighting/ceiling-lighting shows '25 items' but its 25 rows resolve to only 16 distinct productId values (each color-led duplicate card links to the same product page with a different ?Color= query param); /shop/home/lighting/outdoor shows '19 items' -> 8 distinct products; /shop/home/all-decor/mirrors shows '5 items' -> 4 distinct products. Per Rule 1 (exhaustion-check via unique product IDs, do not trust a raw platform total) every qty in this file is the DEDUPLICATED distinct-productId count, not the on-page 'N items' text, with both numbers given in evidence. PAGINATION CEILING (why 6 of 12 rows are null): each category page's SSR payload caps at 30 product rows (pagination.limit=30); when pagination.hasMore=true the remaining rows load via a client-side JS fetch to a private api.onequince.com endpoint. Tried: direct GET with ?cursor=30/?page=2/?offset=30/?widget-<id>=30 (server ignores all, returns page 1 identically); the Next.js data route (/_next/data/<buildId>/....json?cursor=30) also ignored the cursor; api.onequince.com has no discoverable public unauthenticated route (404 'no Route matched'); the Algolia index found has no collection/URL-slug attribute to filter by (checked all hit fields), so it cannot reproduce the curated collection membership either. Browser automation is disallowed by this project's Rule 2. Result: for any category where hasMore=true (total >30 color-variant rows), the true distinct-product count cannot be fully verified from the visible ~30 rows alone, so qty=null+MANUAL REVIEW per THE ONE RULE, with the partial dedup count from the visible rows given as a floor in the flag text. SCOPE - EXCLUDED: Bedding, Furniture, Rugs, Curtains (all-decor/curtains and top-level), Travel, Bags & Accessories, Jewelry, Beauty & Wellness, Gifts (all non-home departments); within Home: Cookware, Bakeware, Table Linens, Kitchen Tools & Cutlery, Flatware Sets, Kitchen Electrics, Caviar, Wine (kitchen appliances/cutlery/bar tools/food+drink consumables); Bath Towels & Bundles, Luxury Robes, Shower Curtains, Bath Mats, Baby & Kids Towels (all textile) and Bathroom Accessories (2 distinct products, a rattan hamper and a rattan accessories set - storage, not decorative, excluded per 'bathroom furniture/storage/fixtures/plumbing' rule); Throws & Blankets, Pillow Covers (textile); Home Fragrance/candles (scented, explicit exclusion); Storage & Organization (baskets/boxes - functional storage, excluded consistent with this project's West Elm precedent); Holiday Decor (explicit NEVER-EXTRACT category); Ceiling Fans (explicit exclusion, both the standalone Lighting>Ceiling Fans node and the 1 ceiling-fan product folded into the Outdoor Lighting collection). MIXED ROLL-UPS HANDLED: Outdoor Lighting collection mixes genuine outdoor lighting with 1 ceiling-fan product ('Outdoor Transitional Ceiling Fan') - dropped per Rule 0/exclusion list, not padded; qty is lamps+sconces only (7 of 8 distinct products). Decorative Objects and Serveware were also observed (in their visible 30 rows) to mix in out-of-scope items (Decorative Objects: 1 faux olive tree, storage baskets/boxes; Serveware: wood conditioner, serving-utensil sets/cutlery) - both rows are null+flagged anyway for the pagination-ceiling reason above, so no exact in-scope count could be finalized; a manual reviewer completing these should drop those out-of-scope titles too. RULE 0.6 DUPLICATE URL: /shop/home/mirrors and /shop/home/all-decor/mirrors are two distinct canonical URLs serving the IDENTICAL 4-product mirror listing (same productIds, same total). Kept the all-decor/mirrors URL (matches the live Decor nav breadcrumb) as the row; the /shop/home/mirrors alias was dropped as a duplicate listing under a second URL, not a second row. JUDGMENT CALL: 'Coffee Table Books' (10 distinct leather-bound decorative books, e.g. '100 Hikes of a Lifetime Leather Bound Book') was kept as a Home Accessories row - these are merchandised purely as coffee-table styling objects (matching leather covers, sold as a decor line), analogous to this project's West Elm 'Books & Bookends' precedent; flag this row if the project wants a stricter books exclusion. No clock category exists on Quince (site search for 'clock' returned zero matching product titles). STATUS: set to 'partial' per this project's convention (S.N. 86/97/118/191) because 6 of 12 leaf rows are null+flagged (the pagination-ceiling issue affects exactly half the in-scope categories: Table & Floor Lamps, Wall Art, Decorative Objects, Dinnerware, Serveware, Glassware) even though every null decision is individually well-verified.
